channel.title: The Diff: AI dev news, only what is verified
channel.description: Every issue of The Diff. What went viral in AI dev tools, and what nobody has noticed yet.

item.title: No. 021: The compression library inside half the internet had a critical hole, and the fix took eight months to ship because nobody knew it was a security bug.
item.description: HTTP2Shell’s Brotli fire drill, Kimi K3.1 Pro, the Hexacon iPhone jailbreak, OpenAI’s no-internet training room, Dessa, 3d-model-anything and hatchzip.

item.title: No. 020: A certificate authority’s private key turned out to be the number 4. The board’s answer: quit the CA business entirely.
item.description: Anthropic’s formal-verification run, banks blocking AI agents at the login, WorldTUI, eMudhra’s exit, reylo, NCM and Snapintosh.

item.title: No. 019: The worst PHP bug in a decade was found by an AI on August 19. The patches, the exploits and the AI-written checker all landed yesterday.
item.description: PHP2Shell, a poisoned LiteLLM release, Claude Duet, a Railway breach, a test key shipped in mitmproxy and the boring patches that matter.

item.title: No. 018: DeepSeek always kept the engine that runs its models in-house. Yesterday it handed everyone the keys.
item.description: DeepInfer open-sourced, eight eMudhra keys proven compromised by signature, Voxtral 3, 333 malicious Tor exits, curl’s public triage and 50,000 fake stats ChatGPT keeps citing.

item.title: No. 017: For weeks a free model called Space Bunny quietly burned through 200 trillion tokens. This morning it got a name.
item.description: MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mistral's Timestral, Mercury 3, recursive harnessing, a site that audits lab scores and a Meta engineer's black box.

item.title: No. 016: An agent told to chase a refund it cannot get starts emailing the council, the press and fourteen law clinics.
item.description: The impossible-refund eval, DeepSeek's search API, silent vector thinking, a git hook quiz, an anti-LLM language and a macOS OpenGL break.

item.title: No. 015: A Saturday email tells 1.4% of OpenCode Console users to rotate their keys.
item.description: The OpenCode breach, OpenAI's rogue agents, DeepSeek 1017, a breakable C64 and a browser ESP32.

item.title: No. 014: A 28-year-old crypto riddle falls to a timestamp.
item.description: The NIST seed bounty, Postgres 19 slipping on AI review, a Home Assistant opt-in fight, a 37-year-old OpenBSD bug and a $20 TPM bypass.
